root.name: Dutch Defense: Krause Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. c4 Nf6 3. Nc3 d6 4. Nf3 Nc6

overview: Black plays the Dutch with 4...Nc6, planning ...e5 in the Staunton style while keeping the f5 pawn. White replies with d5 or e3 and a normal development. The position has unbalanced Dutch features: White has central space, Black the kingside initiative and e5 break. The main-line order I'm unsure of.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with d5 or e4
Develop with e3, Be2 and castle

black_ideas.idea: Strike with ...e5 and use the f-pawn
Put pieces on the kingside and aim at e4

typical_structures.structure: Dutch structure with ...f5 and ...d6 and the ...e5 break

character.notes: Dutch lines lead to unbalanced play where both players take risks.

soundness.notes: A sound if less common Dutch line.

structure.notes: The centre is undecided at this point.

approach.notes: Played at times by strong players, though not the main Dutch set-up.

character.reason: The Dutch tends to give unbalanced positions and mutual risks.

approach.reason: Played now and then at strong level.

level.reason: Understanding of Dutch plans over memorisation.

plans.reason: The sides fight over central space and the ...e5 break.
